spec_match.rationale: The setup (ellipsis + overflow:hidden + nowrap inputs) matches the feature, but the page asserts the clip-on-focus behaviour from a JS focus event rather than observing it, so it demonstrates the trigger, not the rendered contract.

interactive.rationale: Four real focusable inputs with live state badges and a timestamped focus/blur log — not a static code-card (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises focus-to-see-full-text and blur-to-restore-ellipsis, which is exactly what the page stages.

edge_cases.rationale: Only LTR text-family inputs are covered here (siblings cover RTL/readonly/contenteditable), but the explainer note claims the behaviour applies to textarea while the demo includes none.

conformance.rationale: All 9 assertions pass in Chromium 141, but every one checks prerequisites (ellipsis/clip support, selection APIs, overflow measurability) — none observes the focus-switches-to-clip contract, so a pre-149 browser passes identically (flagged; suite is immutable).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM dump, not chrome-devtools-mcp): layout, ellipsised inputs, badges and the 9/0/0 conformance panel all render; focus/blur interactions and badge transitions were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected demo-telemetry.js covers runtime errors, but the page emits no custom interaction or assertion telemetry for its focus/blur lifecycle.

design_system.rationale: All colours are design-system variables (including a color-mix of --accent-blue), focus outlines are explicit, and no button background is overridden without color.

accessibility.rationale: Inputs are keyboard-reachable with visible focus outlines, but all four share the useless duplicate aria-label 'Input' while the visible field-label divs are not associated, and the badges/log are not live regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: field-rows wrap and the comparison grid collapses at 560px; rendered clean at 1280px headless, but the ≈360px touch viewport was not exercised in this session.

openQuestions.title: Stop hard-coding 'focused — clipping' — measure or honestly label the behaviour
openQuestions.detail: The badge and log claim 'ellipsis → clip (full text visible)' purely because a focus event fired; in any pre-149 browser the page reports the new behaviour while the ellipsis is still visible. This is the probe-can't-return-false anti-pattern. Either derive an observable signal (e.g. caret-navigate programmatically and compare scrollLeft/rendered glyph measurement) or relabel the badge as 'focused — Chrome 149+ clips here (manual observation)'.

openQuestions.title: Give each input a real accessible name tied to its visible label
openQuestions.detail: All four inputs carry aria-label="Input", so a screen-reader user hears four identical fields, while the visible 'text input' / 'email input' labels are unassociated divs. Convert field-label to <label for> or set distinct aria-labels matching the visible text.

openQuestions.title: Flag the conformance suite's missing behaviour contract for human review
openQuestions.detail: The 9 assertions prove prerequisites only; none distinguishes a browser that ships clip-on-interaction from one that does not, so the suite reads as full support everywhere. Existing assertions are immutable — a human should consider an additive assertion (or a documented manual-observation note) covering the actual focused-state rendering change.

openQuestions.title: Add a textarea row or correct the note's claim
openQuestions.detail: The explainer note says the behaviour applies when a user focuses 'an input or textarea', but no textarea appears anywhere in this feature's demos. Add a single-line-styled textarea row here (or in field-types-test) or drop textarea from the claim after verifying against the Chromium change.

openQuestions.title: Announce focus-state changes via a live region
openQuestions.detail: Badge text changes and log appends are visual-only; aria-live=polite on the log (or a visually-hidden status) would make the demonstrated state transitions perceivable non-visually.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot and DOM dump of /v149/clip-text-overflow-on-user-interaction/interaction-demo/ plus the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; in-page panel renders 9 pass / 0 fail / 0 blocked). The page renders cleanly with ellipsised inputs and blurred badges; focus/blur could not be driven headless, so the badge/log transitions are untested here. The main defects are honesty-of-evidence ones: the badge asserts clipping without observing it, and the conformance suite cannot return false on a pre-149 browser.
